extracted.intended_audience: school teachers, school administrators, and prospective textbook authors
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for schoolteachers on what to teach, how to introduce new studies or textbooks, classroom management and relations with employers/parents, and practical methods for sharing instructional experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer improving existing institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Falling in with the regularly organized institutions of the country, and elevating them, is more service to the cause of education than founding some magnificent new establishment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author argues that joining and improving established schools benefits the wider community of teachers and learners more than starting isolated projects which may succeed temporarily but confine the results of labor to the founder's immediate sphere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider the school's real and appropriate object before adding studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider carefully what is the real and appropriate object of your institution. Every thing is not to be done in school. The principles of division of labor apply with peculiar force to this employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only include branches that are suitable to the public institution's limited, specific objects. Much of education rightly remains with parents; schools are an association for a few specific and limited objects best accomplished in assemblies of the young.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep common-school plans simple; focus on basics
rubrics_metrics.description: All will admit that it is highly important that every school should be simple in its plan ... and especially, that the public schools ... should never lose sight of what is, and must be, after all, their great design—teaching the whole population to read, write, and calculate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When considering additions, ask whether they will give the common schools too great a complexity or divert teachers from essential duties; simplicity aligned with core aims is essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only publish a textbook for general use if clearly superior
rubrics_metrics.description: If it is a school-book which you are wishing to introduce, consider well ... whether it is, for general use, so superior to those already published, as to induce teachers to make a change in favor of yours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal methods that work for an author do not necessarily suit general circulation. Many textbooks fail because they fit an author's peculiar method rather than broader practice; don't assume manuscript success implies general adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thoroughly review predecessors and ensure a decided advance
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine all that your predecessors have done before you. Obtain ... all other text books on the subject, and examine them thoroughly. If you see that you can make a very decided advance ... go forward slowly and thoroughly in your work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare a textbook only after exhaustive study of existing works; invest time and labor to create a real improvement—the more effort required to gain eminence, the less likely rivals will overtake you.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt textbooks to the character of teachers and institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider ... the institutions throughout the country, and consider carefully the character of the teachers by whom you expect it to be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A textbook must be usable by the teachers who will implement it. It is absurd to produce a book 'good in itself' but unfit because intended teachers don't know how to use it; design for real users' skills and contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish novelty from intrinsic superiority before recommending innovations
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider carefully whether [a new plan's] success in your hands ... be owing to its novelty and to your own special interest, or to its own innate and intrinsic superiority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If success stems mainly from novelty or personal interest, use the method sparingly to relieve monotony and recommend it modestly as 'one method among others' rather than a universal cure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep a journal of experiments and share them
rubrics_metrics.description: Every teacher should KEEP A JOURNAL of all his plans. In these should be carefully entered all his experiments: the new methods he adopts; the course he takes in regard to difficulties ... and any interesting incidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share the most useful entries via periodicals devoted to education, newspapers' teacher departments, or by reading them at teacher meetings. Such practical reports are valuable and preferable to general speculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teachers must be responsible to employers and under their direction
rubrics_metrics.description: The employed ought always to be responsible to the employers, and to be under their direction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the nature of teaching allows some discretion, ultimate authority rests with committees, trustees, or parents who employ the teacher. Teachers should present suggestions but accept employers' decisions as final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit to employer decisions (or resign) rather than disobey
rubrics_metrics.description: The teacher may ... have his option either to comply with their wishes or to seek employment in another sphere; but while he remains in the employ ... he is bound to yield to the wishes of his employers ... and to submit pleasantly to their direction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If employers insist upon a course a teacher believes wrong, the teacher's options are compliance or resignation; it is not right to continue in employment and deliberately disobey or undermine directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect parental primacy in education
rubrics_metrics.description: Providence has made the parents responsible and wholly responsible for the manner in which their children are prepared for the duties of this life ... unless the manner in which it is exercised is calculated to endanger or to injure the community, there can rightfully be no interference except that of argument and persuasion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parents bear the consequences of their children's education and therefore have rightful authority; teachers should be watchful, seek parents' confidence, and use persuasion rather than unilateral action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use reports of cases to teach practical classroom management
rubrics_metrics.description: There is perhaps no way, by which a writer can more effectually explain his views on the subject of education, than by presenting a great variety of actual cases ... All will however be intended to answer some useful purpose, either to exhibit good or bad management and its consequences ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select common, everyday cases (real or imaginary) to illustrate management, exercises, and human traits in children. These case reports serve as a substitute for experience and can provide practical lessons for teachers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate mistakes from carelessness
rubrics_metrics.description: A wide difference must always be made between mistakes arising from carelessness, and those resulting from circumstances beyond control ... The former are always censurable; the latter never.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praise reasoning that is correct given limited data (example: child confusing 'profit' and 'prophet' due to prior exposure). Censure careless errors but avoid blaming pupils whose mistakes follow logically from insufficient information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt practicable, administratively feasible discipline for tardiness
rubrics_metrics.description: The best plan I can think of, is that all who are tardy should lose their recess. ... There is a great objection to this plan from the fact that a boy is sometimes necessarily absent ... The rule was adopted of requiring all those who were tardy, to remain in their seats during the recess, whether they were necessarily tardy or not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual hearings of excuses are time-consuming and impractical; written excuses inconvenience parents and can be gamed. Choose simple rules that are easy to administer and that reduce the problem even if imperfectly fair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discipline firmly but with gentle manners
rubrics_metrics.description: The possibility of being inflexibly firm in measures, and at the same time gentle and mild in manners and language, is happily illustrated ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforce required measures consistently (e.g., withholding privileges when appropriate) while maintaining calm, kind behavior and avoiding harshness; firmness need not mean harshness—Helen's Lesson demonstrates effectiveness of composed, unyielding response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make teacher meetings practical and focused on school-room business
rubrics_metrics.description: Teacher's meetings will be interesting and useful, when those who come forward in them, will give up the prevailing practice of delivering orations, and come down at once to the scenes and to the business of the school-room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure meetings for practical sharing—reading journals, describing experiments and concrete classroom methods—rather than abstract speeches; small groups meeting regularly to hear each other's journals are recommended.
